135	its class is `1` by `picClass_zero`, which is the fibre class by hypothesis, and its `H¹`
136	vanishes by the lemma above.  No locus, no openness, no spreading-out, and the argument is
137	uniform in `p`. -/
138	theorem subsingleton_h1_residueField_tensor_of_genus_zero
139	    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π) (hg : genus C = 0) (p : PrimeSpectrum B)
140	    (htriv : (D.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).cechPicClass = 1) :
141	    Subsingleton ((datumPair D).H1 ⊗[B] p.asIdeal.ResidueField) := by
142	  refine D.subsingleton_h1_residueField_tensor_of_witness p ⟨0, ?_, ?_⟩
143	  · rw [Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass_zero, htriv]
144	    rfl
145	  · exact subsingleton_h1_divisorSheaf_zero_of_genus_zero hg p.asIdeal.ResidueField
146	
147	/-! ## The engine, and the rank-`1` export -/
148	
149	/-- **The rigid engine at genus `0` on a fibrewise-trivial class**: `H¹(C_B, F_D) = 0` and
150	`H⁰(C_B, F_D)` finite projective over `B`, with the fibrewise clause discharged by the
151	genus hypothesis rather than assumed. -/
152	theorem rigidEngine_of_genus_zero (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π) [IsNoetherianRing B]
153	    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom) (hg : genus C = 0)
154	    (htriv : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum B,
155	      (D.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).cechPicClass = 1) :
156	    Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 1) ∧
157	      Module.Finite B (Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 0) ∧
158	      Module.Projective B (Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 0) :=
159	  datumRigidEngine D hπ fun p =>
160	    D.subsingleton_h1_residueField_tensor_of_genus_zero hg p (htriv p)
161	
162	/-- **`H⁰` HAS STALK RANK `1` AT EVERY PRIME** — `π_*L` invertible, in the rank spelling, for a
163	fibrewise-trivial class on a genus-`0` curve over an arbitrary Noetherian test ring.
164	
165	`rankAtStalk_hModule_zero_eq_one` is applied at `n := 0`: its χ-normalization
166	`χ(𝒪_C) = 1 − n` is `χ = 1`, which `chi_moduleKSheaf` plus `genus C = 0` supplies, and its
167	fibre-degree clause is `classDeg κ(p) 1 = 0`, which is `classDeg_one`.  The five fibre
168	instances are installed by hand — they do not synthesize through the `relCurve` `def`
169	barrier. -/
170	theorem rankAtStalk_hModule_zero_eq_one_of_genus_zero
171	    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π) [IsNoetherianRing B]
172	    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom) (hg : genus C = 0)
173	    (htriv : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum B,
174	      (D.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).cechPicClass = 1)
175	    (p : PrimeSpectrum B) :
176	    Module.rankAtStalk (Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 0) p = 1 := by
177	  haveI : IsIntegral (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField) :=
178	    instIsIntegralBaseChange C p.asIdeal.ResidueField
179	  haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1
180	      (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) :=
181	    instSmoothOfRelativeDimensionBaseChange C p.asIdeal.ResidueField
182	  haveI : QuasiCompact
183	      (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) :=
184	    instQuasiCompactBaseChange C p.asIdeal.ResidueField
185	  haveI : Module.Finite p.asIdeal.ResidueField (Sheaf.HModule
186	      ((relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField).moduleKSheaf p.asIdeal.ResidueField) 0) :=
187	    instModuleFiniteHModuleZeroBaseChange C p.asIdeal.ResidueField
188	  haveI : Module.Finite p.asIdeal.ResidueField (Sheaf.HModule
189	      ((relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField).moduleKSheaf p.asIdeal.ResidueField) 1) :=
190	    instModuleFiniteHModuleOneBaseChange C p.asIdeal.ResidueField
191	  refine D.rankAtStalk_hModule_zero_eq_one (n := 0) hπ ?_
192	    (fun q => D.subsingleton_h1_residueField_tensor_of_genus_zero hg q (htriv q)) p ?_
193	  · rw [chi_moduleKSheaf C, hg]
194	  · rw [htriv p, Nat.cast_zero]
195	    exact classDeg_one _
196	
197	/-! ## The degree spelling is the same hypothesis at genus `0` -/
198	
199	/-- **The degree-`0` spelling implies the triviality spelling**, at genus `0`: a fibre class of
200	degree `0` *is* trivial, by the landed field-level converse
201	`eq_one_of_classDeg_eq_zero_of_chi_one` at `χ = 1`.
202	
203	So the theorems above lose no generality by taking triviality as the hypothesis; what they
204	gain is that the hypothesis is statable without the five fibre instances `classDeg` needs.
205	Consumers holding a degree hypothesis at a prime pass through here. -/
206	theorem fibre_cechPicClass_eq_one_of_classDeg_eq_zero
207	    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π) (hg : genus C = 0) (p : PrimeSpectrum B)
208	    [IsIntegral (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField)]
209	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1
210	      (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of p.asIdeal.ResidueField))]
211	    [QuasiCompact
212	      (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of p.asIdeal.ResidueField))]
213	    [Module.Finite p.asIdeal.ResidueField (Sheaf.HModule
214	      ((relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField).moduleKSheaf p.asIdeal.ResidueField) 0)]
215	    [Module.Finite p.asIdeal.ResidueField (Sheaf.HModule
216	      ((relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField).moduleKSheaf p.asIdeal.ResidueField) 1)]
217	    (hdeg : classDeg p.asIdeal.ResidueField
218	      (D.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).cechPicClass = 0) :
219	    (D.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).cechPicClass = 1 :=
220	  eq_one_of_classDeg_eq_zero_of_chi_one p.asIdeal.ResidueField
221	    (chi_moduleKSheaf_baseChange_eq_one_of_genus_zero C p.asIdeal.ResidueField hg) _ hdeg
222	
223	end BasicOpenCocycleDatum

10	/-!
11	# THE RIGID ENGINE FIRES FROM A `pic⁰` MEMBERSHIP, WITH NO FIBREWISE BINDER LEFT
12	
13	`Picard/Pic0RingDatumEngine.lean` fires the RE-4 rigid engine at genus `0` on a
14	`BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π` under the fibrewise binder
15	
16	  `htriv : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum B, (D.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).cechPicClass = 1`
17	
18	and `Picard/Pic0RingFibrewiseTrivial.lean` proves the corresponding statement for a class in
19	`pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k B)`.  **This file joins the two**: for a cocycle-presented `pic⁰`
20	class the binder is discharged, so the engine's conclusions hold with no fibrewise hypothesis
21	anywhere in the statement.
22	
23	## What had to be written, and why it is not a restatement
24	
25	Three spelling seams, each of which had to be crossed rather than asserted:
26	
27	1. **`relCurveMap` vs the whiskering.**  The engine's base-change naturality
28	   (`cechPicClass_baseChange`) is stated on `relCurveMap C B B'`, which is *defined* as
29	   `(C ◁ overSpecMap B B').left` (`Cohomology/RelativeSectionsLinear.lean:160`); the degree
30	   seam (`Picard/DegreeSeam.lean:81`) is stated on `(C ◁ Over.overSpecMap φ).left`.  The two
31	   `overSpecMap`s are **independent definitions in different namespaces** — the duplicate pair
32	   recorded as `I-0144` — and they agree by `rfl` only when `φ` is the canonical algebra map
33	   `(Algebra.ofId B κ(p)).restrictScalars k`.  `relCurveMap_eq_whiskerLeft_residueField` is
34	   that identification, and everything downstream needs it.
35	2. **Field points vs primes.**  `pic0Subgroup` membership quantifies over `k`-algebra maps
36	   into fields; the engine quantifies over `PrimeSpectrum B`.  A residue field *is* such a
37	   field but the instantiation is a written step, not an observation.
38	3. **Degree vs triviality.**  What the membership gives at a prime is a vanishing `classDeg`;
39	   what the engine wants is a trivial class.  The engine's own
40	   `fibre_cechPicClass_eq_one_of_classDeg_eq_zero` converts one to the other at genus `0`, and
41	   it carries **five fibre instance binders** that do not synthesize through the `relCurve`
42	   `def` barrier; they are installed by hand here, as they are there.
43	
44	## What this buys, stated exactly
45	
46	The remaining distance from a `pic⁰` class over a test ring to *triviality* of that class is
47	now: `H¹(C_B, F) = 0` and `H⁰(C_B, F)` invertible (stalk rank `1` at every prime) **are
48	available**, unconditionally on the class beyond its being degree-zero and presented.  On the
49	**divisor/pushforward route** the step that turns an invertible pushforward into a
50	trivialization of the class is the evaluation map `π^*π_*L → L`, which my search did not find in
51	this tree.
52	
53	**Scope corrected after review.**  An earlier version of this paragraph called that evaluation
54	map "the remaining step" for the ring case as such, and asserted its absence from the sibling
55	project and mathlib as measured.  Both were too strong.  It is the remaining step on *this*
56	route only: `Picard/Pic0VanishingRigidityReduction.lean` reaches the same vanishing through
57	field-point rigidity, which never produces a divisor and so never needs the evaluation map at
58	all.  And I verified absence only in AJCR — not in `Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge`, which has
59	adjunction/counit material, and not in mathlib.
60	
61	## What this does NOT do
62	
63	* **It does not prove the ring case**, and it is not on the shortest route to it.  The
64	  evaluation step above is not built here; a fibrewise-trivial class over a ring need not be
65	  trivial (Traverso–Swan: `Subsingleton (CommRing.Pic (Polynomial A))` fails even *given*
66	  `Subsingleton (CommRing.Pic A)`, measured).  A lane wanting only the vanishing should read
67	  `Pic0VanishingRigidityReduction.lean` first: it reduces the same goal to field-point rigidity
68	  with no cohomology, no pushforward and no divisor.  What *this* file is for is the
69	  pushforward route, where `π_*L` invertible is the object of interest in its own right.
70	* **`IsNoetherianRing B` is inherited**, not introduced: it is the engine's own binder, which
71	  `Cohomology/DatumDescent.lean:547` is designed to remove.  Nothing here re-proves it and a
72	  consumer should remove it through that route.
73	* **The cocycle presentation is a real hypothesis** on the `pic⁰` class, inherited from the
74	  DAT-4 degree seam.  `exists_cechPicClass_eq` produces a datum for any Čech class on `C_B`,
75	  but relating *that* datum's class to the plus-class presentation of a `picEt` element is the
76	  `picEtAffineEquiv`/`unit` seam, and it is assumed here rather than proved.
77	
78	  **What the binder is, exactly, after measurement — and a first answer CORRECTED.**  The
79	  *datum* half is free: `exists_datum_pic0_presentation` below produces a presenting datum for
80	  any class whose affine collapse is `PicEtAff.unit` of *some* relative class (`relPicMk` is
81	  surjective and `exists_cechPicClass_eq` is total over every `k`-algebra).
82	
83	  An earlier version of this paragraph then named ring-level surjectivity of `PicEtAff.unit` as
84	  the remaining brick, on the ground that `PicEtAff.unit_surjective_of_section`
85	  (`Picard/EffectivityClose.lean:141`) is field-only and section-dependent.  **That was wrong**,
86	  and a fresh-context audit caught it: `picEtAffineEquiv_relPicToPicEt`
87	  (`Picard/PicEtUnit.lean:161`) supplies the seam at an **arbitrary test ring**, with no field,
88	  no section and no curve hypothesis, for every class in the range of `relPicToPicEt`.  So the
89	  seam is not the obstruction it was priced as; `presentation_of_relPicToPicEt` below is that
90	  observation made usable, and `rigidEngine_of_relPicToPicEt` fires the engine with the
91	  presentation binder **eliminated** for such classes.
92	
93	  What is genuinely missing is therefore **surjectivity of `relPicToPicEt` onto `picEt`** — that
94	  every étale-plus class over a ring comes from a relative Picard class — which is a different
95	  statement about a different map, and is what a lane wanting these conclusions at an
96	  *arbitrary* degree-zero class should target.  `Pic0ChartPlusFibreProducer.lean:199` calls
97	  membership in that range "honesty" and treats it as a real condition, which is consistent.
98	* **Genus `0` only.**  At positive genus the fibre classes are not trivial.
99	
100	## Main declarations
101	
102	* `AlgebraicGeometry.relCurveMap_eq_whiskerLeft_residueField` — the `I-0144` spelling bridge.
103	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_datum_relPicMk_eq` / `exists_datum_pic0_presentation` — the datum in
104	  the presentation binder is produced, not assumed, at every test ring.
105	* `AlgebraicGeometry.BasicOpenCocycleDatum.htriv_of_pic0` — **the discharge**: the engine's
106	  fibrewise binder, from a cocycle-presented `pic⁰` class.
107	* `AlgebraicGeometry.BasicOpenCocycleDatum.rigidEngine_of_pic0` — the engine's three
108	  conclusions with no fibrewise hypothesis.
109	* `AlgebraicGeometry.BasicOpenCocycleDatum.rankAtStalk_hModule_zero_eq_one_of_pic0` —
110	  **`π_*L` invertible** from a `pic⁰` membership.
111	* `AlgebraicGeometry.P1.rankAtStalk_hModule_zero_eq_one_of_pic0` — non-vacuity at `ℙ¹` over an
112	  arbitrary field.
113	-/

124	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
125	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
126	variable {B : Type u} [CommRing B] [Algebra k B]
127	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite π]

131	/-! ## The spelling bridge (`I-0144`) -/
132	
133	/-- **The two `overSpecMap`s agree at a residue field.**
134	
135	`overSpecMap B κ(p)` (`Cohomology/RelativeSectionsLinear.lean:147`) is built from the
136	`algebraMap`; `Over.overSpecMap φ` (`Picard/RelPicAlgebra.lean:44`) from an arbitrary
137	`k`-algebra map.  These are two independent definitions of the same morphism in different
138	namespaces — the duplicate pair filed as `I-0144` — and at the canonical map
139	`(Algebra.ofId B κ(p)).restrictScalars k` they are definitionally equal.
140	
141	Stated because the engine's base-change lemmas live on the first spelling and the degree seam
142	on the second, so no composition of the two is possible without it. -/
143	theorem relCurveMap_eq_whiskerLeft_residueField (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
144	    (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] (p : PrimeSpectrum B) :
145	    relCurveMap C B p.asIdeal.ResidueField
146	      = (C ◁ Over.overSpecMap
147	          ((Algebra.ofId B p.asIdeal.ResidueField).restrictScalars k)).left :=
148	  rfl
149	
150	/-! ## The datum in the presentation binder is not a real constraint -/
151	
152	/-- **Every relative Picard class over a test ring is presented by a cocycle datum.**
153	
154	`relPicMk` is surjective (`RelPic.lean:75`) and `exists_cechPicClass_eq`
155	(`Cohomology/GluedSheafExtraction.lean:301`) turns the resulting Čech class into a
156	`BasicOpenCocycleDatum` with the same class, at **every** `k`-algebra `B`.
157	
158	This is what makes the presentation binder of the theorems below a condition on the *class*
159	rather than on a choice of datum: a `pic⁰` class that is `PicEtAff.unit` of some relative class
160	at all is presented by some datum, and `exists_datum_pic0_presentation` extracts it. -/
161	theorem exists_datum_relPicMk_eq (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
162	    (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] (π : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite π]
163	    (z : relPic C (overSpec k B)) :
164	    ∃ D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π, relPicMk C (overSpec k B) D.cechPicClass = z := by
165	  obtain ⟨L, hL⟩ := relPicMk_surjective C (overSpec k B) z
166	  obtain ⟨D, hD⟩ := BasicOpenCocycleDatum.exists_cechPicClass_eq (π := π) L
167	  exact ⟨D, by rw [hD, hL]⟩
168	
169	/-- **The presentation binder, in its weakest form**: if the affine collapse of `lam` is
170	`PicEtAff.unit` of *any* relative class, then it is `PicEtAff.unit` of `relPicMk` of some
171	datum's Čech class — which is the hypothesis the theorems below take.
172	
173	So those theorems do not secretly quantify over a lucky datum: the datum is produced, and the
174	surviving hypothesis is the `picEtAffineEquiv`/`unit` seam on `lam` alone. -/
175	theorem exists_datum_pic0_presentation (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
176	    (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] (π : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite π]
177	    (lam : picEt C (overSpec k B))
178	    (h : ∃ z : relPic C (overSpec k B), picEtAffineEquiv C B lam = PicEtAff.unit C B z) :
179	    ∃ D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π,
180	      picEtAffineEquiv C B lam
181	        = PicEtAff.unit C B (relPicMk C (overSpec k B) D.cechPicClass) := by
182	  obtain ⟨z, hz⟩ := h
183	  obtain ⟨D, hD⟩ := exists_datum_relPicMk_eq C B π z
184	  exact ⟨D, by rw [hz, hD]⟩

186	namespace BasicOpenCocycleDatum

188	/-! ## The fibrewise binder, discharged -/
189	
190	/-- **THE DISCHARGE**: the engine's fibrewise binder holds for a cocycle-presented `pic⁰`
191	class, at genus `0`.
192	
193	Composition of three landed steps and the bridge above:
194	`cechPicClass_baseChange` moves the fibre class onto `Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap …)`;
195	the bridge rewrites that as the whiskering the degree seam speaks about;
196	`classDeg_fibre_eq_zero_of_cocyclePresented` gives `classDeg κ(p) = 0` from the membership;
197	and the engine's `fibre_cechPicClass_eq_one_of_classDeg_eq_zero` converts degree `0` to
198	triviality at genus `0`.
199	
200	The five fibre instances are installed by hand — they do not synthesize through the `relCurve`
201	`def` barrier, exactly as `Pic0RingDatumEngine` records. -/
202	theorem htriv_of_pic0 (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π) (hg : genus C = 0)
203	    (lam : pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k B))
204	    (h : picEtAffineEquiv C B (lam : picEt C (overSpec k B))
205	      = PicEtAff.unit C B (relPicMk C (overSpec k B) D.cechPicClass))
206	    (p : PrimeSpectrum B) :
207	    (D.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).cechPicClass = 1 := by
208	  haveI : IsIntegral (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField) :=
209	    instIsIntegralBaseChange C p.asIdeal.ResidueField
210	  haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1
211	      (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) :=
212	    instSmoothOfRelativeDimensionBaseChange C p.asIdeal.ResidueField
213	  haveI : QuasiCompact
214	      (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) :=
215	    instQuasiCompactBaseChange C p.asIdeal.ResidueField
216	  haveI : Module.Finite p.asIdeal.ResidueField (Sheaf.HModule
217	      ((relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField).moduleKSheaf p.asIdeal.ResidueField) 0) :=
218	    instModuleFiniteHModuleZeroBaseChange C p.asIdeal.ResidueField
219	  haveI : Module.Finite p.asIdeal.ResidueField (Sheaf.HModule
220	      ((relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField).moduleKSheaf p.asIdeal.ResidueField) 1) :=
221	    instModuleFiniteHModuleOneBaseChange C p.asIdeal.ResidueField
222	  refine D.fibre_cechPicClass_eq_one_of_classDeg_eq_zero hg p ?_
223	  rw [D.cechPicClass_baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField,
224	    relCurveMap_eq_whiskerLeft_residueField C B p]
225	  exact classDeg_fibre_eq_zero_of_cocyclePresented C lam D.cechPicClass h _
226	
227	/-! ## The engine, with no fibrewise hypothesis -/
228	
229	/-- **The rigid engine from a `pic⁰` membership**: `H¹(C_B, F_D) = 0` and `H⁰(C_B, F_D)` finite
230	projective over `B`, for a cocycle-presented degree-zero class at genus `0`.
231	
232	No fibrewise clause appears in the statement: the hypotheses are the membership, its
233	presentation, and the engine's own `IsNoetherianRing B`. -/
234	theorem rigidEngine_of_pic0 (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π) [IsNoetherianRing B]
235	    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom) (hg : genus C = 0)
236	    (lam : pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k B))
237	    (h : picEtAffineEquiv C B (lam : picEt C (overSpec k B))
238	      = PicEtAff.unit C B (relPicMk C (overSpec k B) D.cechPicClass)) :
239	    Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 1) ∧
240	      Module.Finite B (Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 0) ∧
241	      Module.Projective B (Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 0) :=
242	  D.rigidEngine_of_genus_zero hπ hg (D.htriv_of_pic0 hg lam h)
243	
244	/-- **`π_*L` IS INVERTIBLE, FROM A `pic⁰` MEMBERSHIP** — the stalk rank of `H⁰` is `1` at every
245	prime of the test ring, for a cocycle-presented degree-zero class at genus `0`.
246	
247	This is the cohomological output the classical seesaw argument consumes next.  What it does not
248	supply is the evaluation map `π^*π_*L → L`; see the module docstring. -/
249	theorem rankAtStalk_hModule_zero_eq_one_of_pic0 (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π)
250	    [IsNoetherianRing B] (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom) (hg : genus C = 0)
251	    (lam : pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k B))
252	    (h : picEtAffineEquiv C B (lam : picEt C (overSpec k B))
253	      = PicEtAff.unit C B (relPicMk C (overSpec k B) D.cechPicClass))
254	    (p : PrimeSpectrum B) :
255	    Module.rankAtStalk (Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 0) p = 1 :=
256	  D.rankAtStalk_hModule_zero_eq_one_of_genus_zero hπ hg (D.htriv_of_pic0 hg lam h) p
257	
258	end BasicOpenCocycleDatum

260	/-! ## The presentation binder is FREE for classes from `relPic`
261	
262	The correction recorded in the module docstring, made usable.  `picEtAffineEquiv_relPicToPicEt`
263	(`Picard/PicEtUnit.lean:161`) holds at an arbitrary test **ring**, so for a `pic⁰` class whose
264	underlying `picEt` class comes from `relPicToPicEt` the presentation is not a hypothesis at
265	all — it is produced, and with it the datum. -/
266	
267	/-- **The presentation, produced at a test ring**, for a class in the range of `relPicToPicEt`.
268	
269	No field, no curve section, no `IsProper`-flavoured input beyond the standing binders: the
270	ring-level affine-consistency lemma gives the `unit` form directly, and
271	`exists_datum_pic0_presentation` upgrades it to the datum form. -/
272	theorem presentation_of_relPicToPicEt (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
273	    (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] (π : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite π]
274	    (z : relPic C (overSpec k B)) :
275	    ∃ D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π,
276	      picEtAffineEquiv C B (relPicToPicEt C (overSpec k B) z)
277	        = PicEtAff.unit C B (relPicMk C (overSpec k B) D.cechPicClass) :=
278	  exists_datum_pic0_presentation C B π _ ⟨z, picEtAffineEquiv_relPicToPicEt C B z⟩
279	
280	/-- **`π_*L` IS INVERTIBLE WITH NO PRESENTATION BINDER**, for a degree-zero class coming from a
281	relative Picard class over an arbitrary Noetherian test ring, at genus `0`.
282	
283	This is the form the earlier statements should have had: the only hypotheses left are the
284	membership itself, that the class comes from `relPic` (`hz`), the covering datum and the
285	engine's `IsNoetherianRing`.  The datum is existentially produced rather than supplied.
286	
287	**Non-vacuity of `hz`, stated at the level it is actually known.**  `hz` holds at the trivial
288	class (`map_one`, verified), so the statement is not empty.  Whether it holds at a *non-trivial*
289	degree-zero class is precisely the open surjectivity of `relPicToPicEt` discussed above — the
290	classes satisfying it form the intersection of `pic0Subgroup` with a subgroup, and this file
291	does not measure that intersection.  So: non-vacuous, and non-vacuous at a degenerate value
292	until that surjectivity lands. -/
293	theorem exists_rankAtStalk_hModule_zero_eq_one_of_relPicToPicEt (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
294	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
295	    (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] [IsNoetherianRing B]
296	    (π : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite π] (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom)
297	    (hg : genus C = 0) (lam : pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k B))
298	    (z : relPic C (overSpec k B))
299	    (hz : (lam : picEt C (overSpec k B)) = relPicToPicEt C (overSpec k B) z) :
300	    ∃ D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π,
301	      ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum B, Module.rankAtStalk (Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 0) p = 1 := by
302	  obtain ⟨D, hD⟩ := presentation_of_relPicToPicEt C B π z
303	  exact ⟨D, fun p => D.rankAtStalk_hModule_zero_eq_one_of_pic0 hπ hg lam (by rw [hz]; exact hD) p⟩
304	
305	/-! ## Non-vacuity at `ℙ¹` -/
306	
307	/-- **The invertibility of `π_*L` at `ℙ¹` over an arbitrary field**, with the genus hypothesis
308	discharged by `Curve/P1H1Vanishing.lean`.
309	
310	Recorded because the chain above is worth nothing if its curve hypothesis has no witness; the
311	remaining hypotheses are the membership, its cocycle presentation, the covering map datum and
312	the engine's Noetherian binder — none of them about the genus. -/
313	theorem P1.rankAtStalk_hModule_zero_eq_one_of_pic0 (k : Type u) [Field k]
314	    {B : Type u} [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] [IsNoetherianRing B]
315	    {π : (P1.asOver k).left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite π]
316	    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum (P1.asOver k) B π)
317	    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = (P1.asOver k).hom)
318	    (lam : pic0Subgroup (P1.asOver k) (overSpec k B))
319	    (h : picEtAffineEquiv (P1.asOver k) B (lam : picEt (P1.asOver k) (overSpec k B))
320	      = PicEtAff.unit (P1.asOver k) B
321	          (relPicMk (P1.asOver k) (overSpec k B) D.cechPicClass))
322	    (p : PrimeSpectrum B) :
323	    Module.rankAtStalk (Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 0) p = 1 :=
324	  D.rankAtStalk_hModule_zero_eq_one_of_pic0 hπ (P1.genus_asOver_eq_zero k) lam h p
325	
326	end

9	/-!
10	# A `pic⁰` CLASS OVER A TEST **RING** IS TRIVIAL ON EVERY FIBRE
11	
12	The one surviving instance of the hypothesis both live routes to a `rep` producer pass through
13	is the **ring** case of the degree-zero vanishing:
14	
15	  `∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A], Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k A))`
16	
17	`Picard/Pic0VanishingFieldTest.lean` closed every **field** instance at genus `0`, and
18	`Picard/Pic0VanishingAffineReduction.lean` proved the affine binder *is* the `∀ T` binder.  What
19	separates the two is a rigidity statement over a base ring, and the classical route to it —
20	cohomology and base change — consumes a **fibrewise** hypothesis.
21	
22	**This file supplies that hypothesis, as a theorem rather than a binder.**  For a `pic⁰` class
23	over an arbitrary test ring `A`, at genus `0`:
24	
25	* its restriction along every field point of `overSpec k A` is `1` (`fibre_eq_one`);
26	* its fibre Čech class at every prime `p` of `A` has `classDeg κ(p) = 0`
27	  (`classDeg_fibre_eq_zero_of_cocyclePresented`, via the DAT-4 seam).
28	
29	## SUPERSEDED IN PART — read this before citing the first two theorems
30	
31	A fresh-context audit of this file (accepted in full) established two things about its own
32	content, and both are recorded here rather than in a commit message nobody reads:
33	
34	1. **`Picard/Pic0VanishingRigidityReduction.lean:104` has the same statement at an ARBITRARY
35	   test object.**  `fibre_eq_one_of_mem_pic0Subgroup` is `pic0_fibre_eq_one_of_genus_zero`
36	   without the affineness of the test, by the same `Subsingleton.elim`, and it landed twenty
37	   minutes after this file.  So the first two theorems below are *affine specializations of a
38	   landed more general lemma* and should not be cited as independent results; cite that one.
39	   The residue-field corollary is a one-line instantiation of it too.
40	2. **The lead theorem's proof does not use its own subject.**  `pic0_fibre_eq_one_of_genus_zero`
41	   is `Subsingleton.elim` on the target group, so `lam`, `t` and `pic0Map` appear in the
42	   statement and contribute nothing to the proof — the probe replacing the subject by an
43	   arbitrary element of the target closes identically.  The "mechanism" the docstring below
44	   describes (`pic0Map` landing in `pic0Subgroup` through `degAt_picEtMap`) is work done by the
45	   *type ascription*, not by the proof term.  That is not a defect in the statement, which is
46	   true and is the shape consumers want; it does mean the theorem is cheap, and it was first
47	   presented here as though the mechanism were the content.
48	
49	**What survives as this file's own contribution** is the third theorem,
50	`classDeg_fibre_eq_zero_of_cocyclePresented`: the DAT-4 seam application that turns the
51	membership into a *degree* equation at each prime, which is the spelling
52	`Picard/Pic0RingDatumEngine.lean` consumes.  It is two tactic lines and it is not duplicated.
53	
54	## What consumes this, and in which spelling
55	
56	`Picard/Pic0RingDatumEngine.lean` fires the RE-4 rigid engine on a
57	`BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π` under exactly
58	
59	  `htriv : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum B, (D.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).cechPicClass = 1`
60	
61	and its own `fibre_cechPicClass_eq_one_of_classDeg_eq_zero` converts a *degree-`0`* hypothesis at
62	a prime into that triviality at genus `0`.  So the engine's binder is reachable from a `pic⁰`
63	membership, and this file is the reduction that reaches it: `htriv_of_pic0` composes the two.
64	
65	The residue-field instantiation is written out and is **not** a restatement of the field-point
66	form: `pic0Subgroup` membership quantifies over `k`-algebra maps `A →ₐ[k] K` into fields, and the
67	engine quantifies over primes of `A`.  A prime's residue field is such a `K` and
68	`IsLocalRing.residue ∘ algebraMap` such a map, but the instantiation has to be written for the
69	consumer to fire — recorded because the two spellings look interchangeable and are not
70	(the caveat pic-c raised on `I-1640`).
71	
72	## Why the degree condition is *entirely* consumed here
73	
74	Membership in `pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k A)` is degree vanishing at every field point.  The
75	*triviality* statements spend that binder and return a conclusion with no degree in it, so the
76	distance from them to the ring case carries no Riemann–Roch, no `χ`, no chart and no divisor: it
77	is the pure rigidity implication "trivial at every fibre ⟹ trivial".  That is a repricing of the
78	ring case, not a discharge of it.
79	
80	**Corrected after audit:** this claim is *false about the third theorem*, and an earlier version
81	of this paragraph asserted it of every statement in the file.
82	`classDeg_fibre_eq_zero_of_cocyclePresented` has a degree equation **in its conclusion** — that
83	is its purpose, since the engine's converse consumes a degree — and it takes no `genus C = 0`
84	binder at all, so the sentence "both statements consume `genus C = 0`" was wrong about it as
85	well.  Three of the four theorems consume the genus; the degree one does not.
86	
87	## What this does NOT do
88	
89	* **It does not prove the ring case.**  Fibrewise triviality is strictly weaker than triviality
90	  over `A`: `Subsingleton (CommRing.Pic (Polynomial A))` fails to synthesize even *given*
91	  `Subsingleton (CommRing.Pic A)` (measured, `lake env lean`), so no chart or fibre argument
92	  closes the gap by itself; Traverso–Swan is why.  What closes it is the rigid engine's
93	  invertibility conclusion plus a section, which is another lane's route.
94	* **The `classDeg` statement is conditional on a cocycle presentation** of the class
95	  (`h : picEtAffineEquiv C A lam = PicEtAff.unit C A (relPicMk C _ L)`), because the DAT-4 seam
96	  is.  `fibre_eq_one` is unconditional.
97	* **Nothing here is about positive genus.**  Both statements consume `genus C = 0` through the
98	  landed field-test vanishing; at positive genus the fibre classes are *not* trivial and the
99	  conclusion is false.
100	
101	## Main declarations
102	
103	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0_fibre_eq_one_of_genus_zero` — **the fibrewise triviality**: a `pic⁰`
104	  class over a test ring restricts to `1` at every field point, at genus `0`.
105	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0_fibre_residueField_eq_one_of_genus_zero` — the same at the residue
106	  field of a prime, the spelling the ring-datum engine quantifies over.
107	* `AlgebraicGeometry.classDeg_fibre_eq_zero_of_cocyclePresented` — the fibre Čech class of a
108	  cocycle-presented `pic⁰` class has degree `0` at every prime.
109	* `AlgebraicGeometry.P1.pic0_fibre_eq_one` — non-vacuity: the same at `ℙ¹` over an arbitrary
110	  field, with no hypothesis at all.
111	-/
112	
113	set_option autoImplicit false
114	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
115	
116	universe u
117	
118	open CategoryTheory MonoidalCategory Opposite
119	
120	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
121	
122	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
123	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
124	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
125	
126	noncomputable section
127	
128	/-! ## Fibrewise triviality of a degree-zero class over a test ring -/
129	
130	/-- **A `pic⁰` class over a test RING is trivial at every field point**, at `genus C = 0`.
131	
132	The mechanism is that `pic0Map` *lands in* `pic0Subgroup` at the target test — the degree-zero
133	condition is stable under restriction, definitionally through `degAt_picEtMap`
134	(`Pic0Functor.lean:87`).  At a **field** test the whole degree-zero subgroup is a subsingleton
135	(`subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_overSpec_field_of_genus_zero`), so the restricted class equals `1`
136	there.
137	
138	This consumes the degree binder completely: the conclusion mentions no degree.  It is the
139	fibrewise hypothesis of cohomology-and-base-change, available at genus `0` for *every* class at
140	*every* prime simultaneously — no locus, no openness, no spreading-out. -/
141	theorem pic0_fibre_eq_one_of_genus_zero (hg : genus C = 0)
142	    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] (lam : pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k A))
143	    (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ overSpec k A) :
144	    pic0Map C t lam = 1 :=
145	  @Subsingleton.elim _
146	    (subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_overSpec_field_of_genus_zero C K hg) _ _
147	
148	/-- The same in the underlying `picEt` group: the restricted class is the trivial class. -/
149	theorem picEtMap_pic0_fibre_eq_one_of_genus_zero (hg : genus C = 0)
150	    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] (lam : pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k A))
151	    (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ overSpec k A) :
152	    picEtMap C t (lam : picEt C (overSpec k A)) = 1 :=
153	  fibre_eq_one_of_mem_pic0Subgroup C hg lam K t
154	
155	/-! ## The residue-field spelling: what the ring-datum engine quantifies over -/
156	
157	/-- **The fibrewise triviality at the residue field of a prime.**
158	
159	`Picard/Pic0RingDatumEngine.lean` quantifies its `htriv` binder over `PrimeSpectrum B`, while
160	`pic0Subgroup` membership quantifies over `k`-algebra maps into fields.  A prime's residue field
161	`κ(p)` is a field extension of `k` (through `A`), and the field point of `overSpec k A` at `p` is
162	`Over.overSpecMap` of the composite algebra map — so the two quantifiers match, but only once
163	this instantiation is written.
164	
165	Recorded as its own declaration for exactly that reason: "residue fields are field points" is
166	true and is not a proof that a consumer indexed by primes can fire. -/
167	theorem pic0_fibre_residueField_eq_one_of_genus_zero (hg : genus C = 0)
168	    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] (lam : pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k A))
169	    (p : PrimeSpectrum A) :
170	    pic0Map C (Over.overSpecMap
171	        ((Algebra.ofId A p.asIdeal.ResidueField).restrictScalars k)) lam = 1 :=
172	  pic0_fibre_eq_one_of_genus_zero C hg lam _ _
173	
174	/-! ## The degree of the fibre Čech class -/
175	
176	/-- **The fibre Čech class of a cocycle-presented `pic⁰` class has degree zero**, at every
177	`k`-algebra map into a field — in particular at every residue field.
178	
179	Route: the DAT-4 seam `degAt_of_affineEquiv_eq_unit_relPicMk` (`Picard/DegreeSeam.lean:81`)
180	identifies `degAt lam (Over.overSpecMap φ)` with `classDeg K` of the pulled-back Čech class, and
181	membership in `pic0Subgroup` says the left side is `0`.
182	
183	This is the form a consumer holding a *degree* hypothesis at a prime wants: the ring-datum
184	engine's `fibre_cechPicClass_eq_one_of_classDeg_eq_zero` converts it to triviality of the fibre
185	class at genus `0`. -/
186	theorem classDeg_fibre_eq_zero_of_cocyclePresented
187	    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]
188	    (lam : pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k A)) (L : (C ⊗ overSpec k A).left.CechPic)
189	    (h : picEtAffineEquiv C A (lam : picEt C (overSpec k A))
190	      = PicEtAff.unit C A (relPicMk C (overSpec k A) L))
191	    (φ : A →ₐ[k] K) :
192	    classDeg K (Scheme.CechPic.map ((C ◁ Over.overSpecMap φ).left) L) = 0 := by
193	  rw [← degAt_of_affineEquiv_eq_unit_relPicMk φ (lam : picEt C (overSpec k A)) L h]
194	  exact lam.2 K (Over.overSpecMap φ)
195	
196	/-! ## Non-vacuity: the statements fire at a curve, unconditionally -/
197	
198	/-- **Fibrewise triviality at `ℙ¹`, with no hypothesis.**
199	
200	`Curve/P1H1Vanishing.lean` supplies `genus (P1.asOver k) = 0` over an arbitrary field and
201	`Curve/P1Curve.lean` the three curve binders, so the theorem above applies with nothing left to
202	discharge.  Recorded because a fibrewise hypothesis nobody can instantiate is worth nothing, and
203	this one is instantiated at a real curve over an arbitrary field. -/
204	theorem P1.pic0_fibre_eq_one (k : Type u) [Field k]
205	    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
206	    (lam : pic0Subgroup (P1.asOver k) (overSpec k A))
207	    (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ overSpec k A) :
208	    pic0Map (P1.asOver k) t lam = 1 :=
209	  pic0_fibre_eq_one_of_genus_zero (P1.asOver k) (P1.genus_asOver_eq_zero k) lam K t
210	
211	/-- Non-vacuity of the residue-field spelling at `ℙ¹`. -/
212	theorem P1.pic0_fibre_residueField_eq_one (k : Type u) [Field k]
213	    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
214	    (lam : pic0Subgroup (P1.asOver k) (overSpec k A)) (p : PrimeSpectrum A) :
215	    pic0Map (P1.asOver k) (Over.overSpecMap
216	        ((Algebra.ofId A p.asIdeal.ResidueField).restrictScalars k)) lam = 1 :=
217	  pic0_fibre_residueField_eq_one_of_genus_zero (P1.asOver k) (P1.genus_asOver_eq_zero k) lam p
218	
219	end

7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.FamilyCoboundary
8	
9	/-!
10	# A LOCAL-EQUATION SYSTEM OF UNITS PRESENTS THE TRIVIAL PICARD CLASS
11	
12	`Scheme.LocalEquations.picClass` (`Picard/DivisorClass.lean:238`) is the Čech class of the
13	cocycle of transition units `g x y = eqn x / eqn y`.  The landed API around it computes the
14	class *from* a system in every direction except one: **nothing concluded that a class is
15	trivial**.  The producers of `picClass … = 1` were `picClass_zero` (the zero *divisor*, a
16	different carrier) and `picClass_eq_of_divEq` (which only transports triviality between two
17	systems, never establishes it).
18	
19	This file supplies the missing producer, and it is generic: no curve, no base ring, no
20	degree, no cohomology.
21	
22	  **`eqn x` a unit at every point ⟹ `picClass = 1`.**
23	
24	## The mechanism, and why it is not the obvious `simp`
25	
26	The defining relation `eqn x = g x y · eqn y` (`eqn_restrict_eq`) says exactly that the family
27	`α x := (eqn x)⁻¹` is a **coboundary datum** for the transition cocycle, once every `eqn x` is
28	invertible.  `Scheme.unitsH1_eq_one_of_family` (`Picard/FamilyCoboundary.lean:107`) turns a
29	coboundary datum on a refining family into triviality of the `H¹` class, and here the refining
30	family is the cover itself — index type `X`, opens `d.cover.opens`, refinement `le_rfl`.
31	
32	Two mechanical points, recorded because they cost time and will cost it again:
33	
34	* the family lemma restricts the cocycle along `inf_le_inf le_rfl le_rfl`, so the proof needs
35	  "restriction along `U ≤ U` is the identity".  That is `Scheme.resHom_refl` on sections, but a
36	  `rw` with a `unitsRestrict`-level version **fails to match** — the `le`-witness sits inside a
37	  proof argument and the rewrite motive is not type-correct at `instances` transparency.  The
38	  fix that works is to `have` the identity with the inequality *universally quantified*
39	  (`hself` below), so unification picks the witness rather than matching it;
40	* `Scheme.CechPic.mk_one` supplies the `1` in the class group on the same cover, so the two
41	  sides are `mk` of the same cover and `congr 1` reduces to the `unitsH1` statement.
42	
43	## What consumes it, immediately
44	
45	`Picard/DivisorFamilyDegreeZeroGeneral.lean` proves, over an **arbitrary** test ring, that a
46	degree-`0` certified adaptation has unit equations
47	(`isUnit_eqn_of_isCertified_zero`) and is `DivEq` to the trivial system
48	(`divEq_trivEqns_of_isCertified_zero`).  Until now that chain ended at `DivEq`, i.e. at the
49	*quotient* carrier `DivFam`, and said nothing about the **class** in `CechPic` — which is the
50	object the `pic⁰` vanishing is about.  Composing with the theorem here closes that gap:
51	
52	  **a degree-`0` certified divisor family has trivial Picard class, at every test ring.**
53	
54	That is `picClass_eq_one_of_isCertified_zero` below, and it needs no field, no integrality, no
55	smoothness and no Noetherian hypothesis — it inherits exactly the hypotheses of the landed
56	degree-`0` certificate lemma.
57	
58	## What this does NOT do
59	
60	* **It does not prove the `pic⁰` vanishing over a ring.**  The gap that remains there is the
61	  *converse* production step: given a degree-`0` class on `C_A`, exhibit a certified family
62	  presenting it.  The field case of that is `exists_divFam_divFamDivisor_eq`
63	  (`Picard/DivisorFamilyFieldSurj.lean:147`) and it is field-only; over a ring the section
64	  route (`Picard/DivisorDatumRankOne.lean:248` then
65	  `Picard/SectionsToDivisorsClass.lean:212`) is the live candidate and is not completed here.
66	* It says nothing about `picFromBase` membership, which is the `relPic`-level statement and a
67	  strictly weaker conclusion than `picClass = 1` in `CechPic`.
68	
69	## Main declarations
70	
71	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.LocalEquations.picClass_eq_one_of_isUnit_eqn` — **the keystone**:
72	  unit equations present the trivial class.  Generic in the scheme.
73	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivFamZar.picClass_trivEqns` — the trivial system has trivial class.
74	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.picClass_eq_one_of_isCertified_zero` — **a degree-`0`
75	  certified system has trivial class, at every test ring**.
76	-/
77	
78	set_option autoImplicit false
79	
80	universe u
81	
82	open CategoryTheory Limits
83	
84	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
85	
86	/-! ## The keystone, generic in the scheme -/
87	
88	namespace Scheme.LocalEquations
89	
90	variable {X : Scheme.{u}}
91	
92	/-- **A LOCAL-EQUATION SYSTEM OF UNITS PRESENTS THE TRIVIAL CLASS.**
93	
94	The defining relation `eqn x = g x y · eqn y` says the family `α x := (eqn x)⁻¹` is a
95	coboundary datum for the transition cocycle; `Scheme.unitsH1_eq_one_of_family` on the cover
96	itself (index type `X`, refinement `le_rfl`) converts that into triviality of the `H¹` class,
97	and `CechPic.mk_one` puts the two sides on the same cover.
98	
99	This is the only producer of `picClass … = 1` in the tree that establishes triviality rather
100	than transporting it: `picClass_eq_of_divEq` moves it between systems and `picClass_zero` is
101	about the zero *divisor*, a different carrier. -/
102	theorem picClass_eq_one_of_isUnit_eqn (d : X.LocalEquations)
103	    (hu : ∀ x : X, IsUnit (d.eqn x)) : d.picClass = 1 := by
104	  rw [Scheme.LocalEquations.picClass, show (1 : X.CechPic)
105	      = Scheme.CechPic.mk d.cover 1 from (Scheme.CechPic.mk_one d.cover).symm]
106	  congr 1
107	  refine Scheme.unitsH1_eq_one_of_family d.unitsCocycle (fun x => x) d.cover.opens
108	    (fun _ => le_rfl) (fun x => ⟨x, d.cover.mem_opens x⟩)
109	    (fun x => (hu x).unit⁻¹) ?_
110	  intro x y
111	  -- Restriction along `U ≤ U` is the identity.  The inequality must stay *quantified*: with a
112	  -- fixed witness the `rw` motive is not type-correct at `instances` transparency.
113	  have hself : ∀ (h : d.cover.opens x ⊓ d.cover.opens y ≤ d.cover.opens x ⊓ d.cover.opens y)
114	      (w : Γ(X, d.cover.opens x ⊓ d.cover.opens y)ˣ), X.unitsRestrict h w = w :=
115	    fun h w => Units.ext (X.resHom_refl (w : Γ(X, d.cover.opens x ⊓ d.cover.opens y)))
116	  -- The unit form of `eqn_restrict_eq`: `eqn x = g x y · eqn y` as an identity of units.
117	  have key : X.unitsRestrict (inf_le_left : d.cover.opens x ⊓ d.cover.opens y ≤ d.cover.opens x)
118	        (hu x).unit
119	      = d.ratioUnit x y * X.unitsRestrict
120	        (inf_le_right : d.cover.opens x ⊓ d.cover.opens y ≤ d.cover.opens y) (hu y).unit :=
121	    Units.ext (by
122	      rw [Units.val_mul, Scheme.coe_unitsRestrict, Scheme.coe_unitsRestrict,
123	        IsUnit.unit_spec, IsUnit.unit_spec]
124	      exact d.eqn_restrict_eq x y)
125	  rw [map_inv, map_inv, Scheme.LocalEquations.unitsCocycle_evInf, hself, key]
126	  group
127	
128	end Scheme.LocalEquations
129	
130	/-! ## The degree-`0` consequence, at every test ring -/
131	
132	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
133	variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
134	variable {pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsAffineHom pi]
135	
136	/-- **The trivial system has trivial Picard class.**  Its equations are literally `1`. -/
137	theorem DivFamZar.picClass_trivEqns : (DivFamZar.trivEqns C R).picClass = 1 :=
138	  Scheme.LocalEquations.picClass_eq_one_of_isUnit_eqn _ fun y => by
139	    rw [DivFamZar.trivEqns_eqn]
140	    exact isUnit_one
141	
142	/-- **A DEGREE-`0` CERTIFIED SYSTEM HAS TRIVIAL PICARD CLASS, AT EVERY TEST RING.**
143	
144	`isUnit_eqn_of_isCertified_zero` (`Picard/DivisorFamilyDegreeZeroGeneral.lean:125`) spends the
145	degree-`0` rank clause on making every *chart* equation a unit; `eqn_rel` then makes the
146	system's own equations units on the piece overlaps, which is what
147	`divEq_trivEqns_of_isCertified_zero` packages as `DivEq` with the trivial system.  Composing
148	that with `picClass_eq_of_divEq` and the class of the trivial system gives the statement at the
149	level of `CechPic`, which is where the `pic⁰` vanishing lives — the landed chain stopped at the
150	`DivFam` quotient.
151	
152	Hypotheses are exactly the landed lemma's: **no field, no integrality, no smoothness, no
153	Noetherian ring.** -/
154	theorem DivisorAdaptation.picClass_eq_one_of_isCertified_zero
155	    {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations} (A : DivisorAdaptation C R pi d)
156	    (hc : A.IsCertified 0) : d.picClass = 1 :=
157	  (Scheme.LocalEquations.picClass_eq_of_divEq
158	    (A.divEq_trivEqns_of_isCertified_zero hc)).trans DivFamZar.picClass_trivEqns

9	/-!
10	# S11 with the datum SUPPLIED from the vanishing, not assumed alongside it
11	
12	`Albanese/Genus0Terminal.lean` closes the uniqueness half of the frozen
13	`exists_unique_ofCurve_comp` in the degenerate case, and every one of its statements takes a
14	`(d : JacobianData C)` as its first argument.  That binder is not free: `JacobianData` is the
15	Wave-4 north star.
16	
17	`Picard/Pic0VanishingRoute.lean` produces a `JacobianData` from the *same* vanishing hypothesis
18	that `Genus0Terminal`'s theorems already assume.  Feeding it to those theorems supplies the
19	binder from the hypothesis already in hand, so the chain below needs no datum from elsewhere.
20	
21	## Two things a draft of this header claimed and I have deleted (`I-1575`)
22	
23	Both were wrong in the direction that flatters this file, which is the direction nobody checks.
24	
25	* It said the `AJCR.w6-albanese.genus0` row **prices the leaf as gated behind `divRep`**, and
26	  that this file refutes that.  The row does not.  It opens with `GATE WAS INHERITED FOLKLORE`,
27	  carries `depends_on: []`, and states that D6 gates the `Sym^g` fork and not this leaf; its only
28	  "far gate" text is a *quotation* of the worksheet, presented as the thing being refuted — in
29	  run 0078, by a different argument.  **The row already agrees**, and arguing with it was the
30	  overclaim.
31	* It said **"the datum binder and the vanishing hypothesis were never independent"**, and that a
32	  file assuming both assumes the second twice.  False.  `Genus0Terminal`'s theorems hold at an
33	  *arbitrary* `d`.  The statements below instantiate at one carrier, and their conclusions' types
34	  mention `(jacobianData_of_vanishing C h).J`, so a consumer holding a *different* datum cannot
35	  use them.  The binder is **instantiated, not removed** — this is the
36	  `d := Over.mk (𝟙 (Spec k))` face of a strictly more general theorem, not a strengthening of it.
37	
38	So read the declarations below as: *at this carrier*, the S11 chain runs from the vanishing
39	alone.  That is smaller than "the leaf is ungated" and it is what is proved.
40	
41	## What is unconditional here, and what is not
42	
43	Unconditional given the vanishing: existence of the datum, terminality of its representing
44	object, and the uniqueness clause of the Albanese property.
45	
46	**Still open, and it is the same debt `Genus0Terminal` names:** the vanishing itself.
47	`genus C = 0 → pic0Subgroup C T = ⊥` is real curve theory and no declaration in this tree
48	proves it.  Nothing below weakens that; what changes is that the vanishing is now the *only*
49	input, where before it was the vanishing *plus* a datum.
50	
51	Note what has changed *around* it, though, because it decides where to attack the implication:
52	its antecedent is no longer out of reach.  `Curve/P1Curve.lean` supplies the three curve binders
53	at `P1.asOver k` and `Curve/P1H1Vanishing.lean` proves `genus (P1.asOver k) = 0` there, for an
54	arbitrary field — so the implication now has a concrete instance to be proved *at*, rather than
55	only a variable `C`.  What it needs at that instance is the relative statement
56	`Pic(ℙ¹_T) ≅ Pic(T) × ℤ`; a base-field-only computation would not discharge the `∀ T` binder.
57	
58	Also still open, and equally unchanged: the *existence* half of the Albanese `∃!`, which is
59	Milne I 3.9.  It appears as the explicit `hex` hypothesis, exactly as upstream.
60	
61	## Main declarations
62	
63	* `AlgebraicGeometry.jacobianData_of_vanishing` — the datum from `pic0Subgroup C T = ⊥`, i.e.
64	  in the spelling `Genus0Terminal` uses.
65	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isTerminal_jacobianData_of_vanishing` — that datum's representing object is
66	  terminal.
67	* `AlgebraicGeometry.existsUnique_ofCurve_comp_of_vanishing` — **S11's uniqueness clause running
68	  from the vanishing alone**, at this carrier.
69	-/
70	
71	set_option autoImplicit false
72	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
73	
74	universe u
75	
76	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
77	
78	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
79	
80	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
81	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
82	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
83	
84	noncomputable section
85	
86	variable (C) in
87	/-- **The datum, from the `= ⊥` spelling of the vanishing.**
88	
89	`Genus0Terminal` states its hypothesis as `pic0Subgroup C T = ⊥`; the producer in
90	`Pic0VanishingRoute` takes the `Subsingleton` form.  They are interderivable
91	(`subsingleton_of_pic0Subgroup_eq_bot`), so this is the producer in the spelling the
92	consumers below want. -/
93	def jacobianData_of_vanishing
94	    (h : ∀ T : Over (Spec (.of k)), pic0Subgroup C T = ⊥) :
95	    JacobianData C :=
96	  jacobianData_of_subsingleton C fun T => subsingleton_of_pic0Subgroup_eq_bot (h T)
97	
98	variable (C) in
99	/-- **Terminality of the datum built from the vanishing.**
100	
101	`JacobianData.isTerminal_of_pic0Subgroup_eq_bot` concludes `IsTerminal d.J` from a datum `d`
102	plus the vanishing.  Here the datum comes from the vanishing, so no `d` is assumed.
103	
104	Cheap, and honestly so: the representing object is `Over.mk (𝟙 (Spec k))` by construction, so
105	`Over.mkIdTerminal` proves the same goal directly.  The composite is kept because it is the
106	upstream theorem *applied*, which is the check that the producer's output is admissible input
107	there — a statement can be sorry-free and have no site (`I-1463`). -/
108	def isTerminal_jacobianData_of_vanishing
109	    (h : ∀ T : Over (Spec (.of k)), pic0Subgroup C T = ⊥) :
110	    IsTerminal (jacobianData_of_vanishing C h).J :=
111	  JacobianData.isTerminal_of_pic0Subgroup_eq_bot _ h
112	
113	end
114	
115	variable (C) in
116	/-- **S11's uniqueness clause with the datum supplied rather than assumed.**
117	
118	`JacobianData.existsUnique_ofCurve_comp_of_pic0Subgroup_eq_bot` is the upstream assembly; it
119	takes a datum, the vanishing, surjectivity of the curve's structure morphism, a rational
120	point, and the existence half `hex`.  This is the same theorem with the datum *built from the
121	vanishing*, so the hypotheses are: the vanishing, a nonempty curve, a rational point, and `hex`.
122	
123	**Not a generalisation of the upstream theorem** (`I-1575`): that one holds at an arbitrary `d`,
124	and this is its `d := jacobianData_of_vanishing C h` face.  The conclusion's type names that
125	carrier, so a consumer holding a different datum must use the upstream form.  What is bought is
126	that the chain runs from the vanishing alone, with no datum from elsewhere.
127	
128	`hex` is Milne I 3.9 and is still open, exactly as upstream. -/
129	theorem existsUnique_ofCurve_comp_of_vanishing
130	    (h : ∀ T : Over (Spec (.of k)), pic0Subgroup C T = ⊥) (hs : Surjective C.hom)
131	    (P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ C) {A : Over (Spec (.of k))} (f : C ⟶ A)
132	    (hex : ∃ g : (jacobianData_of_vanishing C h).J ⟶ A,
133	      f = (jacobianData_of_vanishing C h).ofCurve P ≫ g) :
134	    ∃! g : (jacobianData_of_vanishing C h).J ⟶ A,
135	      f = (jacobianData_of_vanishing C h).ofCurve P ≫ g :=
136	  JacobianData.existsUnique_ofCurve_comp_of_pic0Subgroup_eq_bot _ h hs P f hex
137	
138	end AlgebraicGeometry

Given a Σ-element `⟨a, ξ⟩` over `T`, the point `a : T ⟶ Spec k` is already a point of the
chart source, and its chart value has Σ-component `a` by
`sigmaComponent_abelSigmaChartZero`.  The two fibre components then live in the same
`pic0Subgroup C (Over.mk a)`, where the hypothesis identifies them — so the transport is
`Over.sigmaExtension_ext` with `Subsingleton.allEq`, and no cohomology, cover or naturality
enters. -/
theorem surjective_app_abelSigmaChartZero_of_subsingleton
    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - ((0 : ℕ) : ℤ))
    (hvan : ∀ S : Over (Spec (.of k)), Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup C S))
    (T : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ) :
    Function.Surjective ((abelSigmaChartZero (C := C) (pi := pi) m Z hdeg).app T) := by
  rintro ⟨a, xi⟩
  refine ⟨a, ?_⟩
  refine Over.sigmaExtension_ext (pic0TypeFunctor C)
    (show a ≫ 𝟙 _ = a from Category.comp_id a) ?_
  exact (hvan _).allEq _ _

omit [GeometricallyReduced C.hom] in
variable (C pi) in
/-- **THE CONVERSE: surjectivity FORCES the vanishing.**

If the chart's app is surjective at the test `S.left`, then every degree-zero class over
`Over.mk S.hom` — i.e. over `S` itself, since `Over.mk S.hom = S` by `rfl` — is the chart
value of some point, and by the previous lemma's Σ-component computation that point is
`S.hom` itself.  So the class is determined, and two classes over `S` coincide.

This is what makes the decision an equivalence rather than a sufficient condition, and it is
the reason this file's headline is not a weakening: a curve with two distinct degree-zero
classes at one test has no hope at this chart, whatever `V` one restricts to
(`not_seamPair_abelSigmaChartZero_of_two_pic0`). -/
theorem subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_of_surjective_app
    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - ((0 : ℕ) : ℤ))
    (hsurj : ∀ T : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ,
      Function.Surjective ((abelSigmaChartZero (C := C) (pi := pi) m Z hdeg).app T))
    (S : Over (Spec (.of k))) :
    Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup C S) := by
  refine ⟨fun x y => ?_⟩
  -- both classes name a Σ-element over `S.left` with structure morphism `S.hom`
  obtain ⟨vx, hvx⟩ := hsurj (op S.left) ⟨S.hom, x⟩
  obtain ⟨vy, hvy⟩ := hsurj (op S.left) ⟨S.hom, y⟩
  -- the Σ-components pin the two points to `S.hom`, hence to each other
  have hx : vx = S.hom := by
    rw [← sigmaComponent_abelSigmaChartZero C pi m Z hdeg S.left vx, hvx]
  have hy : vy = S.hom := by
    rw [← sigmaComponent_abelSigmaChartZero C pi m Z hdeg S.left vy, hvy]
  have : (⟨S.hom, x⟩ : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op S.left)) = ⟨S.hom, y⟩ := by
/-- **THE SHARP FORM: antecedent 2 ALONE is equivalent to the vanishing.**

The pair statement above is not wrong, but it is not sharp: antecedent 1 is a free rider on
both sides of it — unconditional in the forward direction
(`injective_abelSigmaChartZero_sigmaComponent`) and recovered from antecedent 2 in the backward one
(`isOpenImmersion_presheaf_of_injective`).  Stated because the board prices antecedent 2 as
the *most expensive* of the three, so "the pair is decided" would read as a larger discount
than the truth: nothing about antecedent 1 is being bought here, and coverage is the whole
content. -/
theorem isLocallySurjective_abelSigmaChartZero_iff
    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - ((0 : ℕ) : ℤ)) :
    Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology
        (abelSigmaChartZero (C := C) (pi := pi) m Z hdeg)
      ↔ ∀ S : Over (Spec (.of k)), Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup C S) :=
  ⟨fun hcov => (seamPair_abelSigmaChartZero_iff C pi m Z hdeg).mp
      ⟨isOpenImmersion_presheaf_of_injective C _
        (injective_abelSigmaChartZero_sigmaComponent C pi m Z hdeg) hcov, hcov⟩,
   fun hvan => (seamPair_abelSigmaChartZero_of_subsingleton C pi m Z hdeg hvan).2⟩

/-! ## The seam fired, and the arbitrary-parameter form of the repricing -/

omit [GeometricallyReduced C.hom] in
variable (C) in
/-- **THE PRODUCER FIRES.**  Under the vanishing, `pic0TypeFunctor C` is representable.

Stated as an `∃`/`Nonempty` because the representing object `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`
returns is spelled through mathlib's glue data of the very `hf` being supplied, so naming it
in the conclusion would force the reader to reconstruct the term.  What matters is that the
seam machine *runs* on this input: an earlier version of this file claimed
`seamPair_abelSigmaChartZero_of_subsingleton` gave "both antecedents of
`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` at once", which was **false as an applicability claim** — the
producer's antecedent 2 is an instance on `Sigma.desc f`, not on `f`, and `inferInstance` does
not cross that gap.  The `Sigma.ι_desc` factorisation below is the missing line, and this
theorem exists so that the gap cannot silently reopen. -/
theorem exists_representableBy_pic0TypeFunctor_of_subsingleton
    (pi' : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsAffineHom pi']
    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - ((0 : ℕ) : ℤ))
    (hvan : ∀ S : Over (Spec (.of k)), Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup C S)) :
    ∃ J : Over (Spec (.of k)), Nonempty ((pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy J) := by
  set f := fun _ : PUnit.{u+1} => abelSigmaChartZero (C := C) (pi := pi') m Z hdeg with hfdef
  have hpair := seamPair_abelSigmaChartZero_of_subsingleton C pi' m Z hdeg hvan
  haveI : Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f) := by
    haveI := hpair.2
    exact Presheaf.isLocallySurjective_of_isLocallySurjective_fac
      (J := Scheme.zariskiTopology)
      (f₁ := Sigma.ι (fun _ : PUnit.{u+1} =>
        yoneda.obj (Over.mk (𝟙 (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))).left) PUnit.unit)
      (f₂ := Sigma.desc f) (Sigma.ι_desc f PUnit.unit)
  exact ⟨_, ⟨pic0RepresentableByOfCharts C f (fun _ => hpair.1)⟩⟩

variable (C pi) in
/-- **THE REPRICING AT ARBITRARY PARAMETER**, which is what a coverage lane at `n > 0` needs.

`isOpenImmersion_presheaf_of_injective` is stated for an arbitrary presheaf morphism, so it
composes with the *landed* `injective_abelSigmaChart_of_mono` (`Pic0ChartSubsingletonCollapse`)
to give: for the general Abel chart at **any** parameter `n`, with `Mono D.hom` on the
representing object, **coverage implies antecedent 1**.

This is strictly more useful than the parameter-`0` statements above, and it is not about the
terminal chart at all.  A lane holding antecedent 2 at `n > 0` owes `Mono D.hom` and nothing
else on the antecedent-1 side — no `ChartFibrePresented` datum, no relative GAP-2, no
certificate.  `Mono D.hom` is itself a real obligation, and `Pic0ChartForkNegativeBranch`
refutes chart injectivity (hence `Mono`, hence antecedent 1) wherever an effective divisor of
degree `n` has two sections; so this is a reduction of antecedent 1 to a divisor-scheme
property, not a discharge of it. -/
theorem isOpenImmersion_presheaf_abelSigmaChart_of_mono_of_cov {n : ℕ}
    {D : Over (Spec (.of k))} (rep : (divFunctor C pi n).RepresentableBy D) [Mono D.hom]

import Mathlib.Algebra.Polynomial.Module.AEval
import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.TensorProduct.Tower
import Mathlib.RingTheory.Finiteness.Defs
import Mathlib.RingTheory.Finiteness.Basic

/-!
# RE-4b (algebra half) — transport of `AEval'` chart-lattice finiteness

The rigid engine's chart-lattice finiteness is pinned in the spelling
`Module.Finite R[X] (Module.AEval' e)` (`…RigidEngineLatticeModelHom`). This file provides
the three pure module-algebra transports by which the Layer-2 instantiation discharges it
(`informal/w4-rigid-engine-worksheet.md` §4, RE-4b):

* `AlgebraicJacobian.RigidEngine.aevalCongr` (+ `moduleFinite_aeval'_of_linearEquiv`) —
  transport along an equivariant `R`-linear equivalence (used to move between the twisted
  sheaf's chart sections and the structure-sheaf sections, and along the sections
  base-change equivalence).
* `AlgebraicJacobian.RigidEngine.moduleFinite_aeval'_of_ringHom_finite` — the field-level
  entry point: if `φ : k[X] →+* A` is a finite ring map and the endomorphism `e` acts as
  multiplication by `φ X` (with the `k`-scalar action being multiplication by `φ ∘ C`),
  then the `AEval'` lattice of `e` is `k[X]`-finite. Applied with
  `φ = π^* ∘ (chartSectionsEquiv)⁻¹` this is exactly the E-i input
  `Curve/MapToP1.finite_app_chartOpen`.
* `AlgebraicJacobian.RigidEngine.moduleFinite_aeval'_baseChange` — the relative step: an
  `AEval'`-finite lattice over `k[X]` base-changes to an `AEval'`-finite lattice of the
  base-changed endomorphism over `R[X]`, for any `k`-algebra `R` (finitely many
  generators, coefficients pushed through `Polynomial.map (algebraMap k R)`). Composed
  with `aevalCongr` along `relSectionsBaseChange`, this is "`Γ(V₀ᴿ) ≅ Γ(V₀) ⊗_k R` is
  finite over `R[t]`" — the relative E-i.

No schemes appear in this file (the D1 module-algebra discipline).
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

universe u v

open Polynomial

open scoped TensorProduct

namespace AlgebraicJacobian.RigidEngine

/-! ## Transport along an equivariant linear equivalence -/

section Congr

variable {S : Type u} [CommRing S]
variable {M : Type v} {M' : Type*}
variable [AddCommGroup M] [Module S M] [AddCommGroup M'] [Module S M']

/-- **`AEval'` transport along an equivariant equivalence**: an `S`-linear equivalence
intertwining two endomorphisms induces an `S[X]`-linear equivalence of their `AEval'`
modules. -/
noncomputable def aevalCongr (e : Module.End S M) (e' : Module.End S M')
#### outline

###### GluedSheafEngine 190-235
include hπ in
/-- **The rigid engine on the pinned cocycle datum** (Kleiman 3.10 (v)⟹(i)+(iii),
curve-lite; spec (1d-i), all hypotheses discharged): if every residue-field fibre of
`H¹` of the two-lattice pair of the datum's glued sheaf vanishes (complex form — the
sheaf-level discharge is the W6-full seam), then

* `H¹(C_B, F_D) = 0`,
* `H⁰(C_B, F_D)` is a finite projective `B`-module. -/
theorem datumRigidEngine [IsNoetherianRing B]
    (hfib : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum B,
      Subsingleton ((datumPair D).H1 ⊗[B] p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) :
    Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 1) ∧
      Module.Finite B (Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 0) ∧
      Module.Projective B (Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 0) := by
  haveI := D.moduleFinite_aeval'_pair_t₀ hπ
  haveI := D.moduleFinite_aeval'_pair_t₁ hπ
  haveI := D.projective_sections₀
  haveI := D.projective_sections₁
  haveI := D.projective_sectionsInf
  haveI : Module.Projective B
      ((D.sheaf.obj.obj (op (relCover C B (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀)) ×
        (D.sheaf.obj.obj (op (relCover C B (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁))) :=
    Module.Projective.prod
  exact D.pairData.rigidEngine
    (relCover_isAffineOpen₀ C B (fiberTwoCover π))
    (relCover_isAffineOpen₁ C B (fiberTwoCover π))
    (relCover_sup C B (fiberTwoCover π)) hfib

include hπ in
/-- **The openness export on the datum** (the strata gift): the fibrewise-vanishing
locus of `H¹` of the datum pair is open in `Spec B`. Noetherian-free (COH-1 + RE-2). -/
theorem datumRigidEngine_isOpen_vanishing :
    IsOpen {p : PrimeSpectrum B |
      Subsingleton ((datumPair D).H1 ⊗[B] p.asIdeal.ResidueField)} := by
  haveI := D.moduleFinite_aeval'_pair_t₀ hπ
  haveI := D.moduleFinite_aeval'_pair_t₁ hπ
  exact D.pairData.rigidEngine_isOpen_vanishing
    (relCover_isAffineOpen₀ C B (fiberTwoCover π))
    (relCover_isAffineOpen₁ C B (fiberTwoCover π))

/-- **The module-coefficient clause on the datum** (Kleiman `eq:Q`): on the vanishing
locus, formation of `H⁰(C_B, F_D)` commutes with `⊗_B P` for **every** `B`-module
`P`. -/
noncomputable def datumH0TensorEquiv (hH1 : Subsingleton (datumPair D).H1)
    (P : Type u) [AddCommGroup P] [Module B P] :
    (Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 0) ⊗[B] P ≃ₗ[B]
###### DivisorDatumRankOne 130-175 and 240-270
    Sheaf.h0_congr (presentationSheafIso (D.baseChange L))
  have hformula := h0_gluedSheaf_eq_classDeg_add_chi L P hsubP
  have hPclass : P.picClass = (D.baseChange L).cechPicClass := rfl
  have hint : (Sheaf.h0 (D.baseChange L).sheaf : ℤ) = 1 := by
    rw [h0eq, hformula, hPclass, hg, chi_relCurve hχ L]; ring
  exact_mod_cast hint

/-! ## Σ-RANK1: the rank-1 export on the vanishing locus -/

/-- **Σ-RANK1, the datum-level rank export** (worksheet GAP-3): on the fibrewise
h¹-vanishing locus, at fibre degree `n` with the base χ-normalization `χ(𝒪_C) = 1 − n`,
the datum engine's `H⁰` has stalk-rank exactly `1` at `p`.

`Module.rankAtStalk_eq` reads the rank as the `κ(p)`-dimension of the fibre
`κ(p) ⊗[S] H⁰`; the on-the-nose base change `datumH0BaseChange` identifies this fibre with
`H⁰(C_{κ(p)}, F_{D_{κ(p)}})`, whose dimension is `1` by the fibre computation. The global
fibrewise hypothesis `hfib` supplies finiteness/projectivity (hence flatness) through
`datumRigidEngine`. -/
theorem BasicOpenCocycleDatum.rankAtStalk_hModule_zero_eq_one
    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C S π) [IsNoetherianRing S]
    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom)
    (hχ : Sheaf.chi (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 - (n : ℤ))
    (hfib : ∀ q : PrimeSpectrum S,
      Subsingleton ((datumPair D).H1 ⊗[S] q.asIdeal.ResidueField))
    (p : PrimeSpectrum S)
    [IsIntegral (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField)]
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1
      (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of p.asIdeal.ResidueField))]
    [QuasiCompact
      (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of p.asIdeal.ResidueField))]
    [Module.Finite p.asIdeal.ResidueField
      (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField).moduleKSheaf p.asIdeal.ResidueField) 0)]
    [Module.Finite p.asIdeal.ResidueField
      (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField).moduleKSheaf p.asIdeal.ResidueField) 1)]
    (hg : classDeg p.asIdeal.ResidueField
      (D.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).cechPicClass = (n : ℤ)) :
    Module.rankAtStalk (Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 0) p = 1 := by
  obtain ⟨-, hfin, hproj⟩ := datumRigidEngine D hπ hfib
  haveI := hfin
  haveI := hproj
  have hH1 : Subsingleton (datumPair D).H1 := datum_subsingleton_pairH1 D hπ hfib
  have hfibre : Sheaf.h0 (D.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).sheaf = 1 :=
    D.h0_sheaf_baseChange_eq_one hχ p.asIdeal.ResidueField hg
      (D.datum_subsingleton_h1_baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField hH1)
  calc Module.rankAtStalk (Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 0) p
      = Module.finrank p.asIdeal.ResidueField
  exact G.adaptation.divisorDatum.rankAtStalk_hModule_zero_eq_one hπ hχ hfib p
    (G.classDeg_baseChange_divisorDatum p)

/-- **N3 — the generator kit** (worksheet §2 (N3)): since `H⁰(F_{D_G})` is projective of
stalk-rank `1` on the locus, its `κ(p)`-fibre is nontrivial, so a fibrewise-nonzero
**global** section exists on a basic open `D(f) ∋ p` — the Zariski-local generator
(`Module.exists_fibrewise_tmul_ne_zero_of_projective`, the Nakayama-neighbourhood kit of
`Picard/LocalGenerators.lean`). -/
theorem CertifiedDivisorFamily.exists_fibrewise_generator_divisorDatum
    (G : CertifiedDivisorFamily C S π n) [IsNoetherianRing S]
    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom)
    (hχ : Sheaf.chi (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 - (n : ℤ))
    (hvan : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum S, (DivFam.mk G).toZar.IsH1VanishingAt p)
    (p : PrimeSpectrum S) :
    ∃ f : S, f ∉ p.asIdeal ∧ ∃ q : Sheaf.HModule G.adaptation.divisorDatum.sheaf 0,
      ∀ q' : PrimeSpectrum S, f ∉ q'.asIdeal →
        (q ⊗ₜ (1 : q'.asIdeal.ResidueField) :
            Sheaf.HModule G.adaptation.divisorDatum.sheaf 0 ⊗[S] q'.asIdeal.ResidueField) ≠ 0 := by
  have hfib : ∀ q : PrimeSpectrum S,
      Subsingleton ((datumPair G.adaptation.divisorDatum).H1 ⊗[S] q.asIdeal.ResidueField) :=
    fun q => (G.isH1VanishingAt_toZar_iff q).mp (hvan q)
  obtain ⟨-, hfin, hproj⟩ := datumRigidEngine G.adaptation.divisorDatum hπ hfib
  haveI := hfin
  haveI := hproj
  have hrank : Module.rankAtStalk (Sheaf.HModule G.adaptation.divisorDatum.sheaf 0) p = 1 :=
    G.rankAtStalk_divisorDatum_eq_one hπ hχ hvan p
  -- rank 1 ⟹ the `κ(p)`-fibre is nontrivial
  have hfr : Module.finrank p.asIdeal.ResidueField
      (p.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[S] Sheaf.HModule G.adaptation.divisorDatum.sheaf 0) = 1 := by
    rw [← Module.rankAtStalk_eq]; exact hrank
  haveI : Nontrivial (p.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[S]
      Sheaf.HModule G.adaptation.divisorDatum.sheaf 0) :=
    Module.nontrivial_of_finrank_pos (by rw [hfr]; norm_num)
  have hnt : Nontrivial (Sheaf.HModule G.adaptation.divisorDatum.sheaf 0 ⊗[S]
      p.asIdeal.ResidueField) :=
    (TensorProduct.comm S _ _).toEquiv.symm.nontrivial

#### RelPicCoverInjective 75-95
variable [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] [GeometricallyReduced C.hom]

/-- **Restriction of relative Picard classes to an étale cover is injective** — the
consumable corollary of the (C1) étale-separatedness theorem: two relative Picard
classes over `R` agreeing on a presented étale cover of `Spec R` agree.  This is what
licenses every gluing step of the Layer-2 functor. -/
theorem relPicAlgMap_injective_of_etaleCover (E : Algebra.EtaleCover R) :
    Function.Injective
      (relPicAlgMap C ((Algebra.ofId R E.Carrier).restrictScalars k)) := by
  intro x y h
  apply PicEtAff.unit_injective C R
  rw [PicEtAff.unit_eq_mk C E x, PicEtAff.unit_eq_mk C E y]
  exact congrArg (PicEtAff.mk C E) (Subtype.ext h)

end AlgebraicGeometry
#### PicEtUnit 150-175

/-- **THE CLASS LAW** (DAT-A keystone; the Abel correspondence of worksheet §2.2 step
2): the Picard class of the divisor datum cut out by a germ-regular global section of
the DAT-1 glued sheaf is THE Čech Picard class of the datum's cocycle (stage (1e),
consumed on the nose through `cechPicClass_eq_mk`). -/
theorem sectionLocalEquations_picClass :
    (D.sectionLocalEquations s 𝒲 σ hσ hreg).picClass = D.cechPicClass := by
  change Scheme.CechPic.mk 𝒲
    (D.sectionLocalEquations s 𝒲 σ hσ hreg).unitsCocycle.class = D.cechPicClass
  rw [D.sectionLocalEquations_unitsCocycle s 𝒲 σ hσ hreg]
  exact D.cechPicClass_eq_mk 𝒲 σ hσ

end AffineHom

/-- **Independence of the section and the cover** (refinement/rescaling naturality,
subsumed): the class of the divisor datum cut by ANY germ-regular section of the datum,
on ANY subordinated pointed cover, is the same — both are `D.cechPicClass`. Unit
rescalings and cover refinements of the constructed datum keep the class by the landed
`LocalEquations.picClass_rescale`/`picClass_restrict`. -/
theorem sectionLocalEquations_picClass_congr
    {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsAffineHom π] (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π)
    (s s' : ↥(gluedSubmodule B D.pieces D.unit ⊤))
    (𝒲 𝒲' : (relCurve C B).PointedCover) (σ σ' : relCurve C B → D.index)
    (hσ : ∀ y : relCurve C B, 𝒲.opens y ≤ D.pieces (σ y))
    (hσ' : ∀ y : relCurve C B, 𝒲'.opens y ≤ D.pieces (σ' y))
    (hreg : ∀ (j : D.index) (y : relCurve C B) (hy : y ∈ D.pieces j),
      ((relCurve C B).presheaf.germ (D.pieces j) y hy).hom (D.component s j)
        ∈ nonZeroDivisors ((relCurve C B).presheaf.stalk y))
    (hreg' : ∀ (j : D.index) (y : relCurve C B) (hy : y ∈ D.pieces j),
      ((relCurve C B).presheaf.germ (D.pieces j) y hy).hom (D.component s' j)
        ∈ nonZeroDivisors ((relCurve C B).presheaf.stalk y)) :
    (D.sectionLocalEquations s 𝒲 σ hσ hreg).picClass
      = (D.sectionLocalEquations s' 𝒲' σ' hσ' hreg').picClass := by
  rw [D.sectionLocalEquations_picClass s 𝒲 σ hσ hreg,
    D.sectionLocalEquations_picClass s' 𝒲' σ' hσ' hreg']

/-! ## The A2-bundled wrapper, on the canonical pointed cover -/

section Bundled

variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite π]
variable (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π)

/-- **Fibrewise-nonzero sections cut divisors** (DAT-A + DAT-A2, bundled): over a
Noetherian test ring, a fibrewise-regular global section of the DAT-1 glued sheaf
yields a `LocalEquations` divisor datum on the canonical pointed cover by pieces; its
class is `D.cechPicClass` (`sectionLocalEquationsOfFibrewiseRegular_picClass`). -/
noncomputable def sectionLocalEquationsOfFibrewiseRegular
    [IsNoetherianRing B]
    (s : ↥(gluedSubmodule B D.pieces D.unit ⊤))
    (hfib : ∀ (j : D.index) (p : PrimeSpectrum B), Function.Injective
      ((Scheme.mulSectionEnd B (D.component s j)).rTensor p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) :
    (relCurve C B).LocalEquations :=
  D.sectionLocalEquations s D.pointedCover D.pieceIndex (fun _ => le_rfl)
    (fun j y hy => D.germ_component_mem_nonZeroDivisors s j (hfib j) y hy)

/-- The class law for the A2-bundled wrapper: the fibrewise-regular section cuts a
divisor of class exactly the datum's (1e) class. -/
theorem sectionLocalEquationsOfFibrewiseRegular_picClass
    [IsNoetherianRing B]
    (s : ↥(gluedSubmodule B D.pieces D.unit ⊤))
    (hfib : ∀ (j : D.index) (p : PrimeSpectrum B), Function.Injective
      ((Scheme.mulSectionEnd B (D.component s j)).rTensor p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) :
    (D.sectionLocalEquationsOfFibrewiseRegular s hfib).picClass = D.cechPicClass :=
  D.sectionLocalEquations_picClass s D.pointedCover D.pieceIndex (fun _ => le_rfl) _

end Bundled

end BasicOpenCocycleDatum

end AlgebraicGeometry

variable {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations} (A : DivisorAdaptation C R pi d)

/-! ## The constant family lies in the glued equalizer -/

/-- **`1` is always a glued section.**  The two arrows of the equalizer are induced by
*algebra* maps `colength → ovlColength`, so both send the constant family `1` to `1`.  No
hypothesis on the equations, the degree, or the ring. -/
theorem one_mem_gluedSubmodule : (1 : A.chartProd) ∈ A.gluedSubmodule := by
  rw [A.mem_gluedSubmodule_iff]
  intro p
  change A.toOvlLeft p.1 p.2 1 = A.toOvlRight p.1 p.2 1
  rw [map_one, map_one]

/-! ## The unit extraction -/

/-- **A degree-`0` certificate forces every chart equation to be a unit.**

The rank clause read backwards: `Glued` is finite projective of rank `0` at every prime, so
it is a subsingleton (`Module.rankAtStalk_eq_zero_iff_subsingleton`); the constant family `1`
lies in it (`one_mem_gluedSubmodule`); therefore `1 = 0` in each `colength j`, i.e. the ideal
generated by `eqn j` is everything.

This is where degree `0` is spent, and it is spent on *nothing else* — no field, no
integrality, no smoothness, no divisor theory. -/
theorem isUnit_eqn_of_isCertified_zero (hc : A.IsCertified 0) (j : A.index) :
    IsUnit (A.eqn j) := by
  haveI := hc.finite_glued
  haveI := hc.projective_glued
  haveI : Module.Flat R A.Glued := Module.Flat.of_projective
  haveI : Subsingleton A.Glued :=
    Module.rankAtStalk_eq_zero_iff_subsingleton.mp (funext fun p => hc.rankAtStalk_glued p)
  -- the constant family, as an element of `Glued`, is `0`
  have h0 : (⟨(1 : A.chartProd), A.one_mem_gluedSubmodule⟩ : A.Glued) = 0 :=
    Subsingleton.elim _ _
  have hj : (1 : A.colength j) = 0 := congrFun (congrArg Subtype.val h0) j
  rw [← Ideal.span_singleton_eq_top (x := A.eqn j), Ideal.eq_top_iff_one]
  have hmk : Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span {A.eqn j}) 1 = 0 := hj
  exact Ideal.Quotient.eq_zero_iff_mem.mp hmk

/-! ## From unit equations to divisor equality with the trivial system -/

/-- **A degree-`0` certified system is divisor-equal to the trivial one.**

The common refinement is the *piece* cover: at each point `y` pick a piece containing it
(`FinCoverData.exists_mem_pieces`) and intersect with `d.cover.opens y`.  On that open,
`eqn_rel` says `eqn j = u · d.eqn y` with `u` a unit, and `isUnit_eqn_of_isCertified_zero`
says `eqn j` is a unit, so `d.eqn y` is a unit there — and `trivEqns` carries the section
`1`, so the comparison unit is `(d.eqn y)⁻¹`.

Note what does *not* appear: no degree of a divisor, no effectivity, no field.  The
`Subsingleton` results below are corollaries of this one. -/
theorem divEq_trivEqns_of_isCertified_zero (hc : A.IsCertified 0) :
    Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq d (DivFamZar.trivEqns C R) := by
  classical
  choose piece hpiece using A.toFinCoverData.exists_mem_pieces
  refine ⟨⟨fun y => A.pieces (piece y) ⊓ d.cover.opens y,
      fun y => ⟨hpiece y, d.cover.mem_opens y⟩⟩,
    fun y => inf_le_right, fun y => le_top, fun y => ?_⟩
  -- `d.eqn y` restricted to the piece overlap is a unit
  obtain ⟨u, hu⟩ := A.eqn_rel (piece y) y

/-- **Functoriality of the degree at field points** (restriction form): the degree of a
restricted class at a field point is the degree of the original class at the composed
field point.  Pure `picEtMap_comp` rewriting — this is what makes the stability of the
degree-zero subfunctor definitional. -/
theorem degAt_picEtMap (f : T' ⟶ T) (lam : picEt C T) (t' : overSpec k K ⟶ T') :
    degAt (picEtMap C f lam) t' = degAt lam (t' ≫ f) := by
  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t' (picEtMap C f lam)))
      = PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C (t' ≫ f) lam))
  rw [← picEtMap_comp]

/-- Functoriality of the degree at field points, functor form. -/
theorem degAt_picEtFunctor_map (f : T' ⟶ T) (lam : picEt C T)
    (t' : overSpec k K ⟶ T') :
    degAt ((picEtFunctor C).map f.op lam) t' = degAt lam (t' ≫ f) :=
  degAt_picEtMap f lam t'

end DegAt

/-! ## The degree-zero subfunctor -/

variable (C) in
/-- **The degree-zero subgroup** of the étale Picard group of a test object: the
classes of degree zero at every field point of the test.  The object part of the
degree-zero Picard functor `pic0Functor` (gap G-D7). -/
def pic0Subgroup (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) : Subgroup (picEt C T) where
  carrier := {lam | ∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T),
    degAt lam t = 0}
  one_mem' := by
    intro K _ _ t
    exact degAt_one t
  mul_mem' := by
    intro a b ha hb K _ _ t
    rw [degAt_mul, ha K t, hb K t, add_zero]
  inv_mem' := by
    intro a ha K _ _ t
    rw [degAt_inv, ha K t, neg_zero]

/-- Membership in the degree-zero subgroup: degree zero at every field point. -/
theorem mem_pic0Subgroup_iff {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} {lam : picEt C T} :
    lam ∈ pic0Subgroup C T
      ↔ ∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T),
          degAt lam t = 0 :=
  Iff.rfl
